recap:
BHA's Calculated Control Edges Out Everton in a Tight Battle.

BHA managed possession at 47.4%, slightly behind Everton's 52.6%, but their defensive pressure was sharper, with a PPDA of 7.6, significantly lower than Everton's 12.1. Control was maintained across the match, with BHA's field tilt at 64.6% compared to Everton's 35.4%. The game plan largely held, especially regarding set pieces, where BHA won the first contact 50% of the time.

The match was defined by BHA's ability to transition from defensive pressure into scoring chances. The moment that ultimately decided the result was the second goal at minute 63. BHA's #5 Isaac Kane-Moss scored from a set piece, a header with an xG of 0.37, assisted by #7 Tomas Calloway. This goal capitalized on structured attacking routines, proving that when the game plan is executed, opportunities are created.
